about: Team tooling incidents, one record per root cause. Evidence kinds: commit (sha on main), event (seq in .fw-console/events.jsonl, local-only), ci (GitHub Actions run id), file (repo path), proc (process shape, no pids that matter later). Each incident names the work-graph task that fixes it (fix.task, plus fix.also); status is derived, never stored: fixed iff fix.task and every also task are done, fixing iff one of them is claimed, else open (Fw.Plan.Incident; check with pnpm fw incidents lint, see README.md). Each incident also carries its mistake-retro link (research/mistakes/ledger.json): leanVerdict (provable | partly | no), leanReason, hardening (a work-graph task id; required unless the verdict is no), empiricalCheck (the test or CI check; required when the verdict is no), mistakeClass (a retro class id) and mistake (the retro row, informational).

incidents.title: fw land took about 2 minutes for weeks, with the land lock held the whole time, and nothing alerted
incidents.symptom: A Lean-touching fw land took about 126 s at the median (check.sh alone: p50 152.8 s, p90 199.8 s over 5 spans of 112.5, 124.1, 152.8, 191.9 and 199.8 s) and main was blocked for all of it. Nobody noticed until timing spans existed.
incidents.cause: MEASURED (mathview profile and land.ts read, research/notes/2026/10-18-land-speed.md): (1) the mathview lint recomputed the library helper collectAxioms from scratch for each of about 4,077 declarations, with its shared cache off because loadExts is false; about 96% of the lint (p50 118.1 s, max 211.7 s over 8 spans) was that; (2) its cache key covers the whole of Fw/**/*.lean, so every land that touches lean/ misses; (3) fw land runs all of check.sh while the land lock is held (land.ts take to release), so the miss sits on main's critical path; (4) Fw.Obs.Timing flagged slow only against a step's own recent window and needed 5 samples, so a step that is slow from its first run never alerted.

evidence.note: span table from .fw-console/timings.jsonl (local-only): fw land / check.sh p50 152,813 ms, mathview lint (miss) p50 118,082 ms, ranked fixes P1-P5
the research note: mathview collectAxioms is 96% of the lint, the lock is held over all checks

incidents.repro: On a Lean-touching branch run `pnpm fw land <branch> --task <id>`: .fw-console/timings.jsonl gets a `fw land / lock held` span of about 2 minutes (before the speed-ups land).
incidents.regression: Fw.Obs.Timing ceilings (landCeilings: fw land / total 30 s, fw land / lock held 5 s) with the theorem land_budget_alert (a non-noisy land over its ceiling is slow with no history), golden packages/contracts/golden/obs/timing.jsonl, and the #guard that replays the three measured check.sh spans as lock-held samples

incidents.title: Every push to a ci/* branch still started 5-7 workflows (about 40 runs for 20 free runners; the lead cancelled 18-24 by hand) after ci-trigger-scope was marked done
incidents.symptom: chromium-counts, gate-gaps, breakpoint-gate and wktr (5 shared macOS slots) started on pushes to ci/integrate-ports-2 and ci/gate-settle that nobody would read; the lead cancelled them one by one.
incidents.cause: CONFIRMED (workflow files and the guard script read at c5442bc): five causes. (1) The on.push.paths filter of the hosting service tests the push diff before..after, and a merge of main into the branch puts main's files in that diff, so the filter matches. (2) The first fix covered 3 of 11 workflows; later workflows (gate-gaps, difftest, mutants, premise-tests, snapshot-extract, sim-speed) each got a hand-written list and nothing compared the set of workflows with a decision. (3) Every lane that builds fwcore listed lean/**, so an edit to a Lean test, script or part module started them all, though only the import cone of Main.lean can change the binary. (4) The guard job added later (4 macOS lanes) asked whether the whole branch since the merge-base touches an input, so once a branch had touched one every later push started it again. (5) No lint: a trigger could differ from any intent without a check failing.

evidence.note: the first fix: paths filters, 3 workflows
starts_iff, none_started, merge_starts_nothing, filter_passes, skipped_replays; the table of all triggers
the generator and lint of on.push, the guard job and needs

incidents.repro: Push a ci/* branch that merges main, or push twice to a branch whose first push changed lean/: before the fix chromium-counts, gate-gaps, breakpoint-gate and wktr start on the second push.
incidents.regression: packages/contracts/golden/ci/triggers.jsonl (Lean-generated cases), scripts/ci-paths.test.mjs, apps/runner/test/ci-triggers.test.ts (a land check: a workflow whose on.push, guard job or needs differs from the Lean decision fails)
incidents.leanReason: Fw.Ci.Trigger starts_iff, none_started, merge_starts_nothing: a workflow starts iff a push file that differs from main is in its declared inputs; a merge of main starts nothing. The import cone and the YAML are glue, checked by the lint against the Lean table.

incidents.cause: INFERRED (lead's mistake list; harness behaviour of `&` in a foreground call): a trailing `&` detaches the child from the tool call, so nothing holds a handle, a bound or an end signal for it. The sanctioned forms (run_in_background, or a monitor with an until predicate) are prose rules; nothing refuses a long-runner launched with `&`.

incidents.title: Four land waiters deadlocked for about 20 minutes: each waited with pgrep -f on the queue script's name and matched the others
incidents.symptom: The lead started four shell waiters of the form `while pgrep -f "<scratchpad>/land-queue.sh"; do sleep N; done; fw land ...`. None ever left its loop, and no land ran for about 20 minutes.
incidents.cause: CONFIRMED (pgrep(1) on macOS: only the caller and its ancestors are excluded from the match): each waiter's own shell command line contains the pattern text, so every waiter matched the other waiters' shells and all four waited for each other. Process identity came from a command-line pattern, not from a recorded PID, a lock holder or a queue file.

evidence.ref: 4 zsh waiters, each running `while pgrep -f <pattern>` with the pattern in its own argv
evidence.note: process shape seen by the lead
c-identity-heuristic: identity from argv text; the wt-prep pattern defect of the same kind

incidents.repro: Start two shells that each run `while pgrep -f 'x-queue.sh'; do sleep 5; done` (the pattern is in their own argv): neither ever exits.
incidents.regression: none yet: policy-from-lean puts the pgrep -f wait in its golden of violating commands; proposed land-queue replaces shell waiters with one queue file and the land lock
incidents.leanReason: Fw.Ops.Policy (policy-from-lean, kill_iff_owner): a process is selected only by a recorded PID or lock holder, never by a pattern; a queue file with FIFO order under one lock has no wait-for cycle. Proposed task land-queue (not yet in the work graph) adds the queue; policy-from-lean hosts it until then.

incidents.title: Parallel tasks rewrote the same findings ledger entry (hero.exit), so two merges needed manual resolution
incidents.symptom: wktr-p1p4, hero-exit-restate and main each changed the hero.exit entry of research/findings/ledger.json. The ledger merge driver refused both merges, correctly, and the lead unioned the arrays and chose the mechanism text by hand (212c919, dc1fee1).
incidents.cause: CONFIRMED (scripts/merge-ledger.mjs: union by id, a conflict when one id changed differently on both sides): the driver resolves edits to different ids, not two edits to one id. A findings entry holds one shared mechanism string that every task rewrites, and no task owns an entry, so parallel tasks collide on it.

merge main into hero-exit-restate: hero.exit resolved by hand again

incidents.leanReason: With append-only per-task notes keyed by (entry id, task), the id-keyed merge (conflict iff one key changed differently on both sides) never conflicts across tasks.
